entity_ranked_evidence.title: First tranche of NCR’s P85 daily wage hike starts July 25 - Cebu Daily News
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: MANILA, Philippines — Workers in the National Capital Region began receiving the first tranche of the P85 daily **wage hike** on Saturday, July 25. The first tranche of Wage Order No. NCR-27 grants Metro Manila minimum wage earners a P60 increase in their daily wage. This will bring the daily minimum salary for the non-agriculture sector to P780, and P743 for those in the agriculture sector, service and retail shops with 15 or fewer employees, and manufacturing firms with fewer than 10 employees. With this, the Department of Labor and Employment (Dole) said that this wage hike is the “largest in Metro Manila to date,” where 1.1 million workers are expected to benefit from. Despite the call of a non-government organization Foundation for Economic Freedom to the government to suspend the implementation of the wage order, the Palace earlier said that it will not defer the wage hike.

HETAUDA, Nepal (AP) — Associated Press reporter Kristen Gelineau, who has been covering the impact of U.S. foreign aid cuts, reported and wrote the story of how the cuts have prompted scores of unemployed aid workers in Nepal to turn to sex work to survive. While looking into the impacts of the USAID cuts across Asia, an HIV researcher in Nepal mentioned in passing something that I found startling: The leader of an NGO focused on HIV prevention had told him that many of their former workers who had once helped marginalized groups like sex workers had been forced to turn to sex work themselves to survive.

entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: Louisiana and Mississippi farmers face unprecedented losses from Tropical Storm Arthur. Raney Rapp,Senior Staff Writer,Farm Press. Tropical Storm Arthur dumped more than 29 inches of rain in 24 hours across Louisiana and Mississippi, leaving hay fields submerged and cattle farmers facing total losses. Unlike row crop producers, many forage growers lack insurance coverage to recover from flood damage, making this growing season’s losses particularly devastating.Raney Rapp. Flood damage after Tropical Storm Arthur in Avoyelles and St. Landry parishes in Louisiana, as well as counties across the state line in Mississippi, left many farmers questioning how to carry on in a growing season that sorely needed success. The University of Arkansas’ guide “Flood Damage and Recovery Management for Forages” offers a roadmap for recovery after a flood, especially during peak growing season. Raney joined the Delta Farm Press team as a staff writer in 2024 to continue her goal of giving greater voice to farmers’ stories and struggles.

entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: Public File 89.1 WBOI. # Ronan, the Fort Wayne Zoo's harbor seal, died this week. 89.1 WBOI | By Rebecca Green. One of the Fort Wayne Zoo’s harbor seals has died. On Monday, Ronan’s care team noticed he was unresponsive and in need of emergency medical attention. Ronan has only been at the zoo since November 2024, and made his public debut last year. Zoo officials say he quickly became a guest favorite. He was the first harbor seal for the Fort Wayne Zoo. Executive director Rick Schuiteman said that Ronan “served as an ambassador for harbor seals, creating meaningful connections alongside the California sea lions that encouraged curiosity, compassion, conservation –and a lot of smiles as he swam through his habitat.”.
